title: Black hole radial geometry from a quantum spin chain
abstract: We show that the radial differential equation for a scalar field in an anti-de Sitter black brane background can be encoded in an exactly solvable semi-infinite spin chain independent of dimensionality. The radial coordinate emerges as lattice quasimomentum. Spin coherence encodes the geometry, while the spectrum and response recover gravitational observables and yield exact screening-mass sum rules. We implement the finite chain on a superconducting processor. At finite filling and low energies, the model yields a conformal field theory in a coordinate proportional to proper radial distance.
summary: This work demonstrates a profound connection between gravity in Anti-de Sitter space and quantum many-body physics by encoding the radial geometry into a solvable spin chain model. By simulating this chain on a quantum processor, the authors successfully extract gravitational observables, such as the time to the black hole singularity, validating the holographic principle in a quantum computing setting.
main_problem: The paper establishes a dictionary showing how the radial differential equation for a scalar field in an AdS black brane background can be mapped onto an exactly solvable semi-infinite quantum spin chain.
main_result: The model successfully reproduces key gravitational observables, such as the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the proper time to the singularity, using quantum mechanical calculations.
method: The authors use spectral analysis, mapping the continuum differential equation to a discrete spin chain Hamiltonian, and employing techniques like analytic continuation and fitting to extract geometric information.
model_or_system: The system is an AdS black brane geometry dual to a scalar field, whose radial dynamics are encoded in a nearest-neighbor, number-conserving spin chain Hamiltonian. This chain is simulated on a superconducting quantum processor.
key_observables: Screening spectrum, radial coordinate emergence from quasimomentum, thermal one-point function coefficient c(h), and the ratio R(h) used for phase fitting.
important_parameters: The dimensionality $d$, the black brane proper radial distance $\ell$, and the ratio $	au_s/R$ (compared to the exact value $\pi/4$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the continuum problem to a discrete chain, and the final results are subject to finite-size and finite-time simulation errors.
figures_summary: Figures compare the measured quantum propagator evolution against exact theoretical limits, showing the reconstruction of the coefficient c(h) and the phase fit for the radial time scale $	au_s/R$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the mapping from the radial equation to the spin chain, then calculating spectral sum rules, and finally using experimental simulation and analytic continuation to reconstruct the geometric observables like the proper time to the singularity.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable realization of the AdS/CFT correspondence, linking bulk gravity dynamics (black holes) directly to measurable quantum many-body physics on superconducting qubits.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of the dictionary between the black brane geometry and the spin chain. The dimensionless radial coordinate w runs from the d-dimensional boundary (w = 0) to the horizon (w = 1), with w > 1 corresponding to the black hole interior. In the asymptotic regime, the radial coordinate is mapped onto the spin-chain quasimomentum. Real q ∈(0, π) describes the black brane bulk, whereas its analytic continuation, q = iκ with κ > 0, describes the black hole interior.
